title: Effects of changing dysfunctional beliefs in avatar-based cognitive therapy for social anxiety
summary: Negative thought patterns play a crucial role in the development and maintenance of various mental disorders, including social anxiety disorder. Current research shows that digital, avatar-based interventions can be helpful in changing such negative thinking patterns and reducing the symptoms of various disorders. The aim of the present study is to investigate the effects of an avatar-based intervention in the presence of symptoms of social anxiety.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
A score above 4 on the Mini-SPIN was used as an inclusion criterion.
The SPIN was used as a disorder-specific screening instrument. A cut-off score of more than 19 was defined to indicate a possibility of social anxiety.
Exclusion criteria:
Participants with visual/hearing impairments or a lack of German language skills were excluded. Participants with previous episodes of psychosis or mania and participants who were undergoing psychotherapeutic treatment.
